consideredAndDeclined.item: The header's D-002 refusal list omits language roles, which D-018 names among the protected sets
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: D-147's adopted entry carries the identical sentence — commands, platforms, deferrals, identity rides, or the SATISFIED-requiring row set. The statement made is true of this act, and an omission from a refusal list asserts nothing false. Charging a draft for reproducing the corpus's own adopted wording would be charging the wrong document.

consideredAndDeclined.item: The condition-4 cell's 3 HARD-BLOCKED does not match a naive count of cells reading exactly HARD-BLOCKED, which is 2
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: The third is DR-G10's HARD-BLOCKED pending selector refresh, and the register has been counting it inside the 3 since before this act. Before and After both say 3, so the act neither introduces nor perpetuates an error of its own. Recording it here so a later reviewer who counts naively does not mistake an inherited convention for a D-157 arithmetic fault.

coordinatorSummary: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Fourteen attacks run, none landed. I did not apply the MF-6; file 08 stands at 6d593a11 at both ends. Custody is clean: subject 4d2cd832 at 0444 unmoved, HEAD never left 2a90e79, governing tree clean, no D-157 heading and C-D157 unused, all five cited files reproduce, and the D-156 commit f58071ac exists as HEAD's parent. The mechanics that make a gate-adding act safe all hold. The condition-4 Before operand reproduces byte-exact and occurs exactly once in live file 08, so the rewrite has one unambiguous target, and all three fenced operands are backslash-free. A segment-level diff of Before against After shows exactly four changes — owners 28 to 29, required 24 to 25 with D-157 appended, the G29 named under D-157 clause, and OPEN 25 to 26 — and no fifth. Every figure reconciles against live counts, including the one that looks wrong on a naive read: 25 OPEN plus 3 HARD-BLOCKED equals 28 only because the register counts DR-G10's qualified HARD-BLOCKED pending selector refresh inside the 3, an inherited convention this act carries through untouched. The new row has 8 fields in header order, its seven classes are set-equal to the first obligation's owns list in the accepted leftover artifact, its owner matches that obligation's proposed owner, its harness cell carries the same identifier Limb B names, and its evidence cell reproduces the v1-slice §7 item 8 law with the not-G21 and not-G23 distinctions. The insertion point is verified against live structure: DR-G28 is the last gate row and the next non-blank line is the Blueprint-readiness heading, with 65 non-gate rows in the preamble as stated. Two attacks were worth running and both failed. Item 5's leftover closure is D-147's adopted formula, scoped by the words for those seven only, with naming kept distinct from execution — and item 6 then declines the stronger claim D-147 could make, correctly holding that gates 2 and 3 do not hold for DR-117 while three classes stay leftover and three stay unnamed. And the header's D-002 refusal list, which omits language roles, turns out to reproduce D-147's adopted sentence verbatim rather than weaken it. Three items are recorded as considered and declined, including the HARD-BLOCKED count, so a later reviewer does not mistake an inherited convention for an arithmetic fault here.
